summary: At just 7.6 square miles, La Habra packs over 60,000 people into a density north of 8,000 per square mile — yet it reads more like a quiet-suburban grid than a compressed urban core, largely because the city sits on the flat northern edge of Orange County right against the Los Angeles County line, with no dramatic terrain breaks or freeway canyons slicing through its interior. That border position matters practically: La Habra Heights rises to the immediate east with its semi-rural hillside lots, and the 57 freeway provides a spine connecting south toward Fullerton and Brea, meaning many households here commute to job centers elsewhere in Orange or LA counties rather than working locally — a bedroom-community pattern reinforced by a median household income of about $98,000 that, against a median home price near $717,000, yields a price-to-income ratio above 7:1, making ownership a genuine stretch without substantial savings or dual incomes. Renters face a more manageable $2,039 median, roughly 25% of that median gross income. Daily life benefits from 9.4 hours of average sunshine and a remarkably mild temperature band — highs averaging 76°F, lows around 55°F — which makes the city's parks and its stretch of the Fullerton Creek Trail usable year-round. The food and retail corridor along La Habra Boulevard offers genuine sit-down variety and independent shops rather than purely chain sprawl, giving the city a main-street identity distinct from neighboring bedroom tracts. La Habra is essentially an affordable-by-Orange-County-standards flatland suburb whose chief tension is geographic convenience versus the reality that most paychecks are earned somewhere else.
